title: $10 billion startup gets SK Hynix backing to build a transformer that does just one thing but exceedingly well
excerpt: Meet the $10.3 billion startup building AI chips that ignore training and focus entirely on inference performance instead
content_html:
• Etched reached a $10.3 billion valuation after securing fresh SK Hynix backing
  • The startup built custom processors specifically for demanding AI inference workloads
  • Etched says conventional GPUs waste power during many inference tasks today

Etched, a US-based AI chip startup, has secured fresh backing from SK Hynix as it hits a $10.3 billion valuation while pursuing processors built specifically for inference workloads.

The company argues that conventional GPUs deliver more computational capability than many inference tasks require, yet offer insufficient memory for increasingly demanding AI models.

Its latest funding will support the production of rack-scale inference systems designed around custom chips, shared memory, and lower power consumption, rather than general-purpose graphics processors.

Etched bets custom inference chips can outperform traditional GPUs

Founded by former Harvard students Gavin Uberti, Robert Wachen, and Chris Zhu, Etched focuses exclusively on AI inference rather than training large language models.

The startup says its systems combine Low Voltage Inference (LVI) technology with Cluster Scale Memory (CSM), allowing processors to access substantially larger shared memory pools than conventional GPUs.

“Today, AI chips can't scale FLOPs without thermal throttling. As FLOPs utilization increases, AI chips draw more power and downregulate clock speed…,” said Chris Zhu

We’ve designed a new architecture to run our chip’s math blocks at under half the voltage of most AI chips. This enables multiple times the FLOPs density of AI chips today.”

The researchers claim that existing processors struggle to increase floating-point performance because higher utilisation raises power consumption and eventually reduces operating clock speeds through thermal limits.

Processors using High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) cannot achieve SRAM-level decoding speeds because memory subsystems and interconnects introduce additional latency during inference workloads.

They therefore created a shared low-latency memory pool connected through what it describes as a proprietary ultra-low-latency, high-bandwidth interconnect to enable faster memory access

“Our HBM/SRAM hybrid design solves both memory capacity and mem2mem latency, enabling high throughput and interactivity simultaneously.

“CSM improves latency and avoids today's cost, reliability, yield, thermal, and compute tradeoffs of SRAM-only chips, 3D DRAM chips, or optics.”

The company also claims many AI models waste time moving data between chips, memory, and networking hardware before processing can continue.

According to Etched, its CSM architecture reduces those delays by minimising additional memory layers during data transfers.

Funding surge accelerates production and global expansion

Etched has attracted funding at a rapid pace, raising $5.4 million in its 2023 seed round, $120 million in 2024, $500 million in 2025, and $300 million in 2026.

Those investments bring total funding to approximately $925.4 million, while the latest financing doubled the company's valuation from $5 billion to $10.3 billion.

The C-round included Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Jane Street, Diffusion, Argo, and SK Hynix, signalling continued investor confidence despite increasing competition within AI hardware markets.

Robert Wachen said, "This round accelerates production of our inference clusters," while confirming an 80,000 sq ft, 10 MW facility opened near Milpitas.

The company now employs more than 400 people, reports customer demand exceeding $1 billion, and has established manufacturing operations in Taiwan.

Etched systems will support conventional large language models, mixture-of-experts architectures, and alternatives including Mamba.

content_html_zh:
• 在获得 SK Hynix 的新支持后，Etched 估值达到 103 亿美元
  • 该初创公司专门为要求苛刻的人工智能推理工作负载构建了定制处理器
  • Etched 称传统 GPU 在当今的许多推理任务中会浪费电量

总部位于美国的 AI 芯片初创公司 Etched 获得了 SK Hynix 的新支持，估值达到 103 亿美元，同时致力于开发专为推理工作负载打造的处理器。

该公司认为，传统 GPU 提供的计算能力超出了许多推理任务所需的能力，但为要求越来越高的 AI 模型提供的内存却不足。

其最新资金将支持围绕定制芯片、共享内存和较低功耗设计的机架级推理系统的生产，而不是通用图形处理器。

Etched 押注定制推理芯片可以超越传统 GPU

Etched 由前哈佛大学学生 Gavin Uberti、Robert Wachen 和 Chris Zhu 创立，专注于人工智能推理，而不是训练大型语言模型。

该初创公司表示，其系统将低电压推理 (LVI) 技术与集群规模内存 (CSM) 相结合，允许处理器访问比传统 GPU 更大的共享内存池。

“如今，人工智能芯片在没有热节流的情况下无法扩展浮点运算。 随着 FLOP 利用率的增加，AI 芯片会消耗更多电量并下调时钟速度……”Chris Zhu 说道

我们设计了一种新的架构，可以以低于大多数人工智能芯片一半的电压运行我们芯片的数学模块。 这使得当今 AI 芯片的 FLOPs 密度提高了数倍。”

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

研究人员声称，现有处理器很难提高浮点性能，因为更高的利用率会增加功耗，并最终通过热限制降低运行时钟速度。

使用高带宽内存 (HBM) 的处理器无法实现 SRAM 级别的解码速度，因为内存子系统和互连会在推理工作负载期间引入额外的延迟。

因此，他们创建了一个共享低延迟内存池，通过专有的超低延迟、高带宽互连进行连接，以实现更快的内存访问

“我们的 HBM/SRAM 混合设计解决了内存容量和 mem2mem 延迟问题，同时实现了高吞吐量和交互性。

“CSM 改善了延迟，并避免了当今纯 SRAM 芯片、3D DRAM 芯片或光学器件的成本、可靠性、良率、散热和计算权衡。”

该公司还声称，许多人工智能模型在继续处理之前浪费了在芯片、内存和网络硬件之间移动数据的时间。

据 Etched 称，其 CSM 架构通过最大限度地减少数据传输期间的额外内存层来减少这些延迟。

资金激增加速生产和全球扩张

Etched 迅速吸引了资金，在 2023 年种子轮融资中筹集了 540 万美元，在 2024 年筹集了 1.2 亿美元，在 2025 年筹集了 5 亿美元，在 2026 年筹集了 3 亿美元。

这些投资使总资金达到约 9.254 亿美元，而最新融资使该公司的估值翻了一番，从 50 亿美元增至 103 亿美元。

C 轮融资的投资方包括红杉资本、Andreessen Horowitz、Jane Street、Diffusion、Argo 和 SK Hynix，这表明尽管人工智能硬件市场的竞争日益激烈，但投资者的信心依然持续。

Robert Wachen 表示，“这一轮加速了我们推理集群的生产”，同时确认在米尔皮塔斯附近开设了一个 80,000 平方英尺、10 兆瓦的设施。

该公司目前拥有 400 多名员工，报告客户需求超过 10 亿美元，并已在台湾建立了制造业务。

Etched 系统将支持传统的大型语言模型、专家混合架构以及包括 Mamba 在内的替代方案。
